title: Standard analytic projective holomorphic module over constant complex coefficients
statement: For $n\in\mathbf N$, let $Q_n=\operatorname{Projectivization}_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf C^{n+1})$ be the quotient of nonzero vectors by nonzero complex scalar multiplication. For $j\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and $w\in\mathbf C^n$, let $v_j(w)$ insert $1$ into position $j$ of $w$, and put $s_j(w)=[v_j(w)]$; the vector $v_j(w)$ is nonzero. A presentation of the standard analytic projective holomorphic module consists of a ringed space $(X,C_X)$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], an identification $e:X\simeq Q_n$ for which $z\mapsto e^{-1}[z]$ is a quotient map from $\mathbf C^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}$, and, on every open $U$, a ring isomorphism $C_X(U)\simeq\operatorname{LocallyConstant}(U,\mathbf C)$ compatible with restriction, using the locally constant functions of [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-maps-presheaf]. It also consists of a sheaf $\mathcal O$ of $C_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with injective additive evaluation maps $\mathcal O(U)\to\{f:U\to\mathbf C\}$. Their ranges are exactly the functions for which, for every $j$ and every $w$ with $e^{-1}s_j(w)\in U$, the coordinate function $w^{\prime}\mapsto f(e^{-1}s_j(w^{\prime}))$ is complex analytic at $w$. This coordinate function is extended by zero when its argument is outside $U$; only germs inside the coordinate domain are tested. Evaluation respects restriction and satisfies $(a f)(x)=a(x)f(x)$ under the coefficient identification. Thus $C_X$ is the constant complex ring sheaf, and $\mathcal O$ is the usual holomorphic function sheaf with its specified scalar action. The zero-dimensional case is included.

source.place: Serre, GAGA, nos. 1--2 (holomorphic function sheaves) and 13, Lemma 4, printed pp.3--5 and 20--21; read online https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1956__6__1_0.pdf.
